data.headline: How mature are Brightwave's operations?
data.intro: Leo, logistics teams your size run on a lot of know-how that sits in a few heads. Three minutes shows which parts are already written down and which are not.

steps.title: Write down the ten decisions a coordinator makes most
steps.body: Ten decisions, one page each. New coordinators ramp faster, and you see which steps a system could take over.

steps.title: Agree on five Monday numbers and one view that holds them
steps.body: Choose the five figures every operations manager reads on Monday, such as cost per load and on-time rate. Build one view for them and retire the spreadsheets that fed the old ones.

steps.title: Put the three most repeated handoffs on rules
steps.body: Pick the three handoffs coordinators repeat most each day, such as load confirmation to carrier update, and let software do them before you add people. At your size this is usually where the first month of time comes back.

steps.title: Name one owner for improvement, with two hours a week
steps.body: One person, a backlog, and a slot every week. It is the cheapest change on this page and it makes the other moves stick.
